--- title: "When to Use Machine Learning Solutions?" description: "Understanding when ML is appropriate and how it compares to other approaches." format: revealjs: html-math-method: plain slide-number: true slide-level: 2 theme: - slides.scss resources: - data/ - img/ editor: render-on-save: true --- # What is Machine Learning (ML)? ## Example: Image classification - Have you used search in Google Photos? You can search for "my photos of cat" and it will retrieve photos from your libraries containing cats. - This can be done using **image classification**, which is treated as a supervised learning problem. ## Image classification - Imagine writing a Python program to differentiate between cats and foxes. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](img/cat-or-fox.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} - How would you approach it with traditional programming? - Would it scale? ::: :::: ## Traditional programming vs. ML {.smaller} - **Traditional programming**: Best when rules are explicit and data is predictable - Example: Finding the shortest path using Dijkstra’s algorithm - **Machine learning**: Useful when rules are hard to define or data is noisy/complex - Example: Distinguishing between images of cats and foxes using patterns learned from data ## What is ML? - ML uses data to build models that identify patterns, make predictions, or generate content - It enables computers to learn from examples - No single model fits all problems # Simple examples of machine learning problems # Supervised Classification ## Example 1: Predicting whether a patient has a liver disease or not {.smaller} - Suppose you have access to the data below: ::: {#0cf1a5ca .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

Clustering/Semantic Search ## Example 5: Finding groups in data ## Example 6: How to find most similar items? # Dealing with sequential data ## Example 7: Time series # Survival Analysis ## Example 8: What's the probability of a customer ending their Netflix service? ## ML vs. Rule-based Systems vs. Human Experts {.smaller} - ML: Complex patterns in large data - Rule-based systems: Structured decision logic - Human experts: Context, ethics, creativity # Interactive: Is ML appropriate? ## Exercise 1.1: ML or not? {.smaller} **Select all that apply: Which problems are suitable for ML?** - (A) Identifying objects in digital images - (B) Providing solutions via a troubleshooting guide - (C) Evaluating eligibility for financial services via strict rules - (D) Detecting fraudulent banking transactions - (E) Analyzing medical images for diagnosis ## Exercise 1.2: Human expert or not? {.smaller} **Select all that apply: Which problems are better handled by human experts?** - (A) Ensuring regulatory compliance - (B) Recommending products based on user history - (C) Evaluating legal cases involving context - (D) Making ethical end-of-life decisions - (E) Providing mental health support ## Summary: When is ML suitable? - ML: Best for complex patterns, large datasets, fuzzy boundaries - Rule-based: Clear, deterministic logic - Human expert: Ethics, creativity, empathy, ambiguity ## Activity 1: ML in Your Domain {.smaller} Think of a problem from your own research that could be solved using ML. Address the following: - What are you trying to accomplish? What would success look like? - How do humans solve this now? Are there heuristics or rules? - What kind of data do you have or could you collect? - What are the features? What could the target be? We'll revisit this activity later to explore how you might frame your problem using supervised learning, unsupervised learning, generative AI, or non-ML approaches. # Examples of ML Problem Types ## Tabular data - **Tabular data**: - Supervised classification (e.g., disease/no disease) - Supervised regression (e.g., price prediction) - Survival analysis (e.g., time-to-event modeling) - **Text data**: - Sentiment analysis, document classification, indexing/search - **Image data**: - Image classification, object detection - **Time series**: - Forecasting, anomaly detection - **Unsupervised learning**: - Clustering, dimensionality reduction - **Recommendation systems**: - User-item matching, personalized content
